stories.headline: US arrests of Sinaloa officials tied to Rocha Moya cartel charges trigger sovereignty crisis and Sheinbaum political response
stories.summary: US authorities detained former Sinaloa state security chief Gerardo Mérida Sánchez in Arizona and former state finance minister Enrique Díaz, both charged with Sinaloa Cartel ties and alleged payments from Los Chapitos. Their detentions—alongside standing charges against Governor Rubén Rocha Moya (Morena)—triggered a major diplomatic and political crisis. Sheinbaum responded with repeated sovereignty declarations ('no corrupt person can hide under the 4T,' 'no foreign government will take the Transformation'), distanced herself from the accused, and disclosed that approximately 50 politicians are under investigation for organized crime links. Sinaloa's interim governor Yeraldine Bonilla claimed SEDENA—not Rocha Moya—appointed Mérida to his state post, a claim SEDENA has not confirmed. Reports also surfaced of possible US custody of Morena Senator Enrique Inzunza, though unconfirmed by official sources.

stories.headline: Morena mobilizes march in Chihuahua against Governor Maru Campos over CIA controversy, threatens impeachment
stories.summary: Morena national leadership—including party president Ariadna Montiel and Andrés Manuel López Beltrán—traveled to Chihuahua to lead a march demanding a juicio político against Governor María Eugenia 'Maru' Campos, framing her as responsible for permitting unauthorized CIA operations in the state. The march, contested in size (Morena claimed 20,000; critics called turnout a failure), was met by counter-protests, highway blockades by farmers, and booing at the airport. Security Secretary García Harfuch had separately denied CIA involvement in a Tecámac explosion. The PAN and PRI condemned the march as political theater covering for Morena's own narco-corruption scandals. The confrontation marked an escalation of the federal-state battle over the CIA-Chihuahua incident.

stories.headline: Sheinbaum inaugurates major hospitals and social infrastructure on Yucatan-Campeche tour
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum conducted a multi-day tour of the Yucatan Peninsula and Campeche, inaugurating the Naval Hospital of Yukalpetén (serving 12,000 SEMAR beneficiaries), the new Hospital General 'Dr. Agustín O'Horán' in Mérida (described as the largest hospital in Latin America), a University Rosario Castellanos campus, a CBTIS vocational school, and a Pasteurizadora Leche para el Bienestar in Campeche. She announced a 181 billion peso hospital investment plan for her administration and oversaw the transfer of the old Naval Hospital facility to ISSSTE. The tour was accompanied by sovereignty rhetoric linked to the Sinaloa crisis and counter-protests by Pemex and CFE retirees opposing pension cuts.

stories.headline: Pemex CEO Víctor Rodríguez replaced by CFO Juan Carlos Carpio amid financial pressures
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum announced the departure of Pemex CEO Víctor Rodríguez Padilla and nominated the company's chief financial officer Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso as replacement, effective immediately. Sheinbaum said Rodríguez had agreed from the outset to serve only 18 months and denied the change was related to a recent hydrocarbon spill in Veracruz. Carpio, an economist with ties to Sheinbaum from her tenure as Mexico City chief, is seen as a continuity pick focused on the company's debt restructuring. The announcement coincided with S&P Global revising Pemex's credit outlook to negative.

stories.headline: S&P downgrades Pemex and CFE outlook to negative; Pemex debt restructured to 2033
stories.summary: S&P Global Ratings revised the credit outlook of both Pemex and CFE from stable to negative, citing persistent fiscal pressure and unsustainable financial structures. Separately, the Cuenta Pública 2025 revealed that Pemex had restructured 67% of its supplier debt—totaling approximately 375 billion pesos—extending payment deadlines to 2033. Analysts at Banamex warned that Moody's may also downgrade Mexico's sovereign rating. Pemex reported improved Q1 2026 refining output (+21.9%) and reduced fuel imports as partial offsets.

stories.headline: Banxico launches 12 World Cup commemorative coins as interest rate cycle closes at 6.50%
stories.summary: The Banco de México released a collection of 12 commemorative coins for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including gold, silver, and bimetallic 20-peso pieces featuring Mexican host cities and cultural motifs; the coins began circulating May 13. Separately, Banxico's rate-cutting cycle concluded with the benchmark rate at 6.50%, triggering debate among analysts and business groups about monetary policy credibility. Governor Victoria Rodríguez Ceja defended the institution's record, saying Banxico was never 'complacent' with inflation. Foreign investors withdrew more than 3.4 billion pesos from Cetes in April amid the rate environment.

stories.headline: Sheinbaum-Trump phone call on security and trade; US officials to visit Mexico
stories.summary: President Sheinbaum held a phone call with US President Donald Trump on May 15, which she described as 'cordial and excellent.' The two leaders discussed security cooperation and bilateral trade, and agreed to continue dialogue. Sheinbaum also indicated that US cabinet members and officials would visit Mexico in the coming days. The call occurred amid escalating tension over the Sinaloa cartel corruption charges and CIA controversy.

stories.headline: García Harfuch leads federal security cabinet meeting in Michoacán to review Plan Michoacán
stories.summary: Secretary of Security Omar García Harfuch traveled to Morelia for a security review meeting with Michoacán Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla and nine municipal mayors, alongside the secretaries of SEDENA and SEMAR. The meeting addressed extortion as the municipalities' principal security concern and reviewed six months of implementation of the Plan Michoacán, which officials said has reduced homicides by 41.8% in the state's first quarter. García Harfuch committed to maintaining federal force levels in the state.

stories.headline: SEMAR dismantles five narco-labs in Jalisco, Nayarit, and Sinaloa linked to CJNG's 'El Jardinero'
stories.summary: The Navy (SEMAR), in coordination with SSPC and the FGR, dismantled five clandestine methamphetamine laboratories across Jalisco, Nayarit, and Sinaloa, seizing more than one metric ton of drugs and precursor chemicals valued at over 650 million pesos. Two of the labs were linked to Audias 'El Jardinero' Flores, identified as a senior CJNG operative. A federal court separately confirmed a judicial suspension blocking El Jardinero's extradition to the United States.

stories.headline: CFE retirees win court suspension against pension cuts as protests follow Sheinbaum on Yucatan tour
stories.summary: A federal collegiate tribunal in Nuevo León granted a provisional suspension ordering the Comisión Federal de Electricidad to immediately halt pension reductions affecting approximately 40,000 retirees, ruling the cuts were equivalent to torture and violated basic human rights. The ruling related to the 'golden pensions' reform enacted by Congress. Separately, Pemex and CFE retirees staged protests at multiple Sheinbaum events in Yucatan, with one retiree personally delivering a document to the president.
